_comment_1: Rule 13(4) LMPC 2011 - dozen, score, gross, great gross.
_comment_2: STEP 2. The clause names the prohibited units verbatim, so detecting them needs no judgement and no applicability input.
_comment_3: DELIBERATELY UNDER-CLAIMS, TWICE. (1) The clause also prohibits units 'or the like', which is open-ended and no list can close - a pass therefore reports only that the NAMED units are absent. (2) It reaches anything 'specified or indicated on any package', but only the net quantity declaration is scanned: matching the whole recognised text would flag 'Gross Weight', which is lawful, and a false violation is worse than an under-claim.
title: No dozen, score, gross or great gross on the package
requirement: The net quantity must not be expressed using a number called the dozen, score, gross or great gross.
legal_reference: Rule 13(4) of the Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011
source_note: Checked 2026-08-30 by Claude Code (automated legal-source check) for raghavrrrao against the Department of Consumer Affairs consolidated publication 'Book on Legal Metrology Packaged Commodities Rules, 2011 with all amendments' (sha256 0ef948f9c6b89f5dfb20d384861901714fd0dc54fc67b5b86c772d2c3f983a4b; server Last-Modified 2025-04-14), via the verbatim quotation recorded in rules/INVENTORY.md. Clause 13(4) reads verbatim: 'No number called the dozen, score, gross, great gross or the like shall be specified or indicated on any package.'
